prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation: the PROTAC concept of directing a protein to a ubiquitin ligase with a bifunctional molecule, and the identification of cereblon as the target through which thalidomide-type molecular glues degrade proteins.

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep B012 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. All eight members ranked it in the opening round, and no colleague has argued that the underlying science is wrong. The disputes concern attribution and timing. What the committee can state in physical terms is that a small molecule can make a ternary complex that does not exist otherwise, and that the cell's own ubiquitin machinery then does the work. The PROTAC lineage shows this by design, and the cereblon lineage shows the same event-driven principle by a drug that reshapes a ligase surface. Both have been reproduced in many laboratories and with many E3 ligases, so maturity is judged by independent confirmation of the mechanism, and I do not require an approved drug for that. I answer the chair's first question directly. If a third seat must be chosen, I would credit Handa over Ciulli, because cereblon is the mechanistic explanation that unites the thalidomide history with the PROTAC field and is the E3 behind most of the clinical programmes. The citation then describes one achievement with two entry routes into a common principle, not two unrelated prizes.
statement.case_against: The strongest case against my position is that it is a compromise forced by the three-person limit. Ciulli's VHL ligands and the structural basis for ternary-complex cooperativity made PROTACs real chemistry rather than peptidic proofs of concept, and Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito also have real claims. A committee that regards the PROTAC and glue lineages as separate achievements would find my citation too wide, and one that wants settled clinical proof would find it early, since no degrader is approved. Aqvist and Somfai also make a fair point that B055 has the cleanest two-name attribution and no maturity question. If the expert reports weighted Ciulli's structural work as decisive, or showed that the two lineages should not share a citation, I would have to reconsider.

responses.point: Heiner asks, as chair and as a B060 supporter, whether base editing can be separated from CRISPR-Cas9 in one citation sentence and whether excluding Kondo and Nishida is acceptable. He also names Ciulli as the better third name for B012.
responses.response: Heiner's sentence is clear and the evolved adenine deaminase is a real chemical contribution, because no natural enzyme existed for it. My difficulty is that the principle is a programmable deaminase delivered by a nuclease the committee already recognised in 2020, and the same function was reported in parallel by Kondo and Nishida, so any three-name list is contestable. I would still treat B060 as the closest second choice and would not exclude Liu from consideration. On Ciulli, I still prefer Handa. VHL ligands and ternary-complex structure refine and optimise a concept, whereas cereblon explains a drug action that had been a mystery for decades. I accept that this is a judgement call that the expert reports should help settle.

responses.point: Johan argues that Buchwald and Hartwig is the only shortlisted candidate with both a clean two-person attribution and no maturity question, and that it is distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
responses.response: I agree that the attribution and the maturity are the strongest on the list, and that is why B055 remains my first alternative. What would still need to be put on the record is what the C-N coupling added conceptually beyond the 2010 prize. Ligand control of oxidative addition and reductive elimination for an N-nucleophile is a real advance, but it is arguably the same catalytic manifold. I do not accept that being overdue is a reason to rank it above a field that introduces a new mode of action, but I accept that it is the safe choice if the committee wants a molecule-making prize this year.

responses.point: Peter Somfai says that Kosugi's tin-amide coupling is a real precursor but that the practical general method is Buchwald and Hartwig, while admitting he is working from memory on how far it anticipated the catalytic cycle.
responses.response: I share the caveat, since the Kosugi history is also known to me only from memory and the files do not settle it. As Secretary I would want the expert report to put the priority evidence on the record before a two-name citation is finalised. If the report shows that Kosugi's work was a narrow, tin-dependent reaction and not the catalytic framework, then the pair is clean. Until then I do not think the priority question is a reason to prefer B055 over B012, because B012 has a comparable attribution problem and I have stated it openly.

responses.point: Daniel proposes the same trio for B012 and notes that the Ciulli and Gray contributions complicate attribution, and that B019 would be the safer choice if settled clinical impact were required.
responses.response: We agree on the configuration, and I accept her point that much of the novelty is in design rather than a new reaction. I would add that it is design resting on a defined physical mechanism, namely ternary-complex formation and cooperativity, and that is the part I value. I keep my view that the prize should not depend on Phase 3 readouts that nobody on the committee has confirmed. On B019, I agree that it is the safest translational option, but its achievement is delivery formulation, and I would not move it ahead of B012 on that basis.

responses.point: Andrei supports Liu, Komor and Gaudelli for B060 and stresses that the Liu laboratory credit is unusually well documented, with the adenine editor as the strongest evidence of originality.
responses.response: I accept that the credit inside the Liu laboratory is documented and that directed evolution of an adenine deaminase is original chemistry. My concern remains the convention of crediting two lead experimentalists beside the principal investigator when an independent parallel group is excluded, and a decade of in vivo safety data is still being built. I would move to B060 if the committee settles on a Liu-led configuration and the reports separate it clearly from the 2020 prize, but I do not do so now.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports treat PROTAC design and cereblon molecular-glue mechanism as one achievement or two.
Whether the Ciulli structural contribution is judged decisive for PROTAC practicality, which would change the third name.
How the Kosugi precursor history weighs against Buchwald and Hartwig, which I know only from memory.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader drug will be weighed more heavily by colleagues than I weigh it.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate or credited name has arisen in the exchange. I serve as Secretary and deputy member of the Nobel Foundation board, which is procedural, and I remain a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, whose field (zeolites, B018) is outside my own work and not part of my configuration.
